crop.notes: Only the first column of the 'Twenty Years a Prize Fighter' feature; the right side of the headline is cut off and the article continues in further columns (see 912-914). Ends mid-sentence after the Bob Smith story.

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Republic profiled Tom Allen, 54, at his Champion's Rest saloon on Market Street, where he argued that old open-air bare-knuckle fighting was safer than the indoor gloved bouts of 1895.

metadata.notes: Masthead: The Republic: St. Louis, Mo., Sunday Morning, March 31, 1895, page 40.

facts.fact: Allen was shot in the back of the right hand during his fight with Charley Gallagher at Chouteau Island, up the Mississippi, in August 1869, leaving a deep scar
In 1895 Allen kept the Champion's Rest saloon on Market Street near Seventh, St. Louis, and lived upstairs with his trophies
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street near Seventh, St. Louis

facts.fact: The English championship cup, won in a fight with Prof. Davis in 1878, was kept in a glass case behind the bar of Champion's Rest; the case had been broken half a dozen times in saloon rows
places: Champion's Rest, Market Street, St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen said open-air bare-knuckle fighting was safer than modern indoor gloved fighting
facts.quote: When we fought in the open, the air was always changing. A man would get a good breath when he was resting, instead of having to breathe the foul stuff that they get to-day.

facts.fact: In England Allen fought Baltimore Bob Smith barefoot in the open country the day after the match was made, and was beaten in fifty minutes
Allen had a brother, Harry, who was a fighter and had twice been beaten by Bob Smith

notes: Allen's own account uses a racial slur for Smith; the quote chosen avoids it. Overlaps with the first column of 912.
